mcqs.learning_point: Understand qualitative statement of second law
mcqs.question: Which of the following best states the qualitative statement of the second law of thermodynamics?

options.A: Heat cannot spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body.
options.B: Energy is conserved in all processes.
options.C: Work can be completely converted into heat.
options.D: The internal energy of an isolated system remains constant.

mcqs.answer: Heat cannot spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body.
mcqs.explanation: The qualitative statement of the second law says that heat naturally flows from a higher temperature to a lower temperature and never the reverse without external work. Option A captures this. Option B describes the first law, C is unrelated, and D is also a statement of the first law (energy conservation).

mcqs.question: Two metal blocks are placed in thermal contact. Block A is at 80 °C and Block B is at 20 °C. In which direction will heat flow spontaneously?

options.A: From Block B (20 °C) to Block A (80 °C)
options.B: From Block A (80 °C) to Block B (20 °C)
options.C: No heat flow will occur because the blocks are in contact
options.D: Heat will oscillate back and forth between the blocks

mcqs.answer: From Block A (80 °C) to Block B (20 °C)
mcqs.explanation: According to the second law, heat flows spontaneously from the hotter body to the colder one. Hence heat moves from the 80 °C block to the 20 °C block. Options A, C, and D contradict this principle.

mcqs.question: A heat engine operates between a source at 500 K and a sink at 300 K. According to the second law, which statement is true about its efficiency?

options.B: Its maximum possible efficiency is (500 K − 300 K) / 500 K = 40 %.
options.C: Its efficiency can exceed 40 % if friction is negligible.
options.D: The efficiency is independent of the temperatures of the source and sink.

mcqs.answer: Its maximum possible efficiency is (500 K − 300 K) / 500 K = 40 %.
mcqs.explanation: The Carnot efficiency gives the upper limit for any engine operating between two reservoirs: η_max = 1 − T_cold/T_hot = (500 − 300)/500 = 0.40 or 40 %. No real engine can exceed this limit, making options A, C, and D incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish reversible and irreversible processes at the required level
mcqs.question: Which of the following processes is irreversible?

options.A: Isothermal expansion of an ideal gas carried out quasistatically with an infinitesimal temperature difference.
options.B: Free expansion of a gas into a vacuum.
options.C: Reversible adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas.
options.D: Slow compression where the external pressure is always equal to the internal pressure.

mcqs.answer: Free expansion of a gas into a vacuum.
mcqs.explanation: Free expansion occurs without external pressure and cannot be reversed without external work; entropy increases, making it irreversible. Options A, C, and D describe quasistatic or reversible processes.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand qualitative statement of second law
mcqs.question: A common misconception is that heat can be completely converted into work without any other effect. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: True, the second law allows 100 % conversion of heat to work.
options.B: False, the second law forbids 100 % conversion of heat into work.
options.C: True, but only when the temperature of the heat source is absolute zero.
options.D: False, but only for irreversible processes.

mcqs.answer: False, the second law forbids 100 % conversion of heat into work.
mcqs.explanation: The second law states that some heat must be rejected to a colder reservoir; therefore 100 % conversion is impossible. Option B correctly addresses the misconception. Options A and C are false, and D misplaces the restriction to only irreversible processes.

mcqs.question: Why does heat flow spontaneously from a hotter body to a colder body?

options.A: Because the entropy of the universe decreases during the process.
options.B: Because the internal energy of the hotter body is higher.
options.C: Because the total entropy of the system plus surroundings increases when heat flows from hot to cold.
options.D: Because a temperature difference creates a magnetic field that drives the flow.

mcqs.answer: Because the total entropy of the system plus surroundings increases when heat flows from hot to cold.
mcqs.explanation: Spontaneous processes occur when the total entropy increases, which is exactly what happens when heat moves from a higher to a lower temperature. Option A is opposite, B is irrelevant to direction, and D is unrelated.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the efficiency of a Carnot engine with that of a real engine operating between the same source and sink temperatures?

options.A: Both have equal efficiency if friction is ignored.
options.B: The Carnot engine has higher efficiency because it is reversible and operates on an ideal cycle.
options.C: A real engine can exceed Carnot efficiency by using regenerative cycles.
options.D: The Carnot engine’s efficiency is lower because it requires more heat input.

mcqs.answer: The Carnot engine has higher efficiency because it is reversible and operates on an ideal cycle.
mcqs.explanation: The Carnot engine represents the maximum possible efficiency for given temperatures; real engines suffer irreversibilities and thus have lower efficiency. Option B captures this. Options A, C, and D are incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish reversible and irreversible processes at the required level
mcqs.question: In an isolated system, which statement correctly distinguishes a reversible process from an irreversible one?

options.A: Both reversible and irreversible processes have ΔS = 0.
options.B: A reversible process has ΔS = 0, whereas an irreversible process has ΔS > 0.
options.C: A reversible process has ΔS > 0, whereas an irreversible process has ΔS = 0.
options.D: Both reversible and irreversible processes have ΔS < 0.

mcqs.answer: A reversible process has ΔS = 0, whereas an irreversible process has ΔS > 0.
mcqs.explanation: For an isolated system, entropy remains constant (ΔS = 0) in a reversible process and increases (ΔS > 0) in an irreversible process. This is a standard criterion used in competitive exams. Options A, C, and D contradict the second law.
